post.description:
Submit quotes using CAIP-2 chain identifiers or existing network IDs. CAIP-2 identifiers must refer to a configured chain. Submissions using unregistered legacy network IDs remain accepted.
    However, for us to actually quote users' intents, the chains need to be enabled by the "LiFi Intent" protocol.
    We periodically update the supported chains, assets, and routes, but if you need a specific chain to be supported, please contact us.

requestBody.description: Submit or update quotes. Each request can contain up to 50,000 quotes and 100,000 ranges in a JSON body up to 32 MiB after decompression. Split larger inventories between routes. Send every range for a route in the same request because a later submission for that route replaces the earlier submission. To remove a quote, send an empty `ranges` array: `"ranges": []`.

post.description: Submit a signed server-issued message to register an account for reputation tracking. Supports EVM ECDSA (EOA), EVM EIP-1271 (smart contract wallet), Solana ed25519, Tron TIP-191, and Stellar SEP-53 signatures. Stellar requires an existing account whose original key meets all thresholds on the configured verification network. Permissions are checked at registration, not continuously. The message must have been obtained from GET /api/v1/solver/register/message. Note: the message is single-use and is consumed on the first POST attempt regardless of outcome. If registration fails, call GET /register/message again before retrying.

Quotes with the account in exclusiveFor may still be accepted for up to 30 seconds after it is removed.

put.description: Replaces the authenticated solver's RFQ chains. The solver gets an RFQ request only when both the source and the destination chain of the request are listed, so a same-chain request needs that chain listed once. The list is optional. A solver with no chains gets RFQ requests on every chain. Send the complete list, or an empty list to get every chain again. If any chain is unsupported, no changes are saved. Changes apply to new RFQ requests within 5 seconds.

get.description: Collects the authenticated solver’s unexpired quote ranges and returns them newest first. Public and integrator-specific books are included. Filters combine with AND and asset-only filters can match several chains. Each cursor continues the same collected listing despite later updates, removals or expiry. A route can span pages. Check validUntil before using a range and finish the traversal before treating the result as a complete inventory. The initial collection reads routes over a short window, not at one atomic instant. To refresh the result, start without a cursor. Collected listings expire. On 410, discard the partial result and start without a cursor. Keep the same filters when continuing. Limit may change between pages.

Only the first leg is represented; an order with further inputs or outputs does not report them here. Null when the leg is missing or the encoding cannot be decoded. A native asset is reported as the native sentinel of that chain, in that same form: the zero address on EVM, its base58check equivalent T9yD14Nj9j7xAB4dbGeiX9h8unkKHxuWwb on Tron, and 11111111111111111111111111111111 on Solana. Only the first leg is represented; an order with further inputs or outputs does not report them here. Null when the leg is missing or the encoding cannot be decoded. A native asset is reported as the native sentinel of that chain, in that same form: the zero address on EVM, its base58check equivalent T9yD14Nj9j7xAB4dbGeiX9h8unkKHxuWwb on Tron, and 11111111111111111111111111111111 on Solana.

receivingTokenAmount.description: Amount encoded on outputs[0], in the smallest unit of the receiving token. Only the first leg is represented; an order with further inputs or outputs does not report them here. For limit orders this is exactly the amount the intent requires to be delivered. For DutchAuction and ExclusiveDutchAuction orders it is the minimum amount: the output settler requires this plus the remaining auction decay, so the amount required at fill time is higher. Never the amount actually delivered, which is not stored. Null when the leg is missing or the amount cannot be read.

fromAsset.description: Source asset identifier. EVM (eip155): 0x-prefixed 40-char hex. Solana: 32–44 char base58. Tron: base58check, T-prefixed, 34 chars. Bitcoin: slip44:0 or slip44:1.

toAsset.description: Destination asset identifier. EVM (eip155): 0x-prefixed 40-char hex. Solana: 32–44 char base58. Tron: base58check, T-prefixed, 34 chars. Bitcoin: slip44:0 or slip44:1.

minAmount.description: Lower bound of the input amount this range applies to. Denominated in `fromAsset` raw on-chain base units (integer scaled by `fromDecimals`). Inclusive — compared directly against the user's `fromAmount`. At most 78 digits.

maxAmount.description: Upper bound of the input amount this range applies to. Denominated in `fromAsset` raw on-chain base units (integer scaled by `fromDecimals`). Inclusive — compared directly against the user's `fromAmount`. At most 78 digits.

quote.description:
Exchange rate for this range — write it like a normal price: `toAsset` per 1 `fromAsset` (e.g. `0.999` = 0.999 USDC per 1 USDT). Do **not** scale for `fromDecimals`/`toDecimals`; the API does that for you.

Full formula:

    outputBase = floor( (inputBase / 10^fromDecimals) * quote * 10^toDecimals )

Example (USDT → USDC, 18 → 6 decimals): for `inputBase = 10^18` (1 USDT) at `quote = 0.999`, the user receives `outputBase = 999000` (0.999 USDC).

Must be greater than zero, with at most 36 integer and 36 fractional digits.

fixedCost.description: The fixed cost to add to the quote in `fromAsset` raw base units. On cross-chain quotes it prices the default oracle and only applies when `oracleCosts` is omitted. On same-chain quotes it covers all local settlement costs.

oracleCosts.description: Fixed costs for the oracle pairs supported by this quote range. Each entry identifies one pair by its contracts on `fromChain` and `toChain`, and gives the total cost in `fromAsset` raw base units. At most 20 entries per range. Cross-chain quotes only: use `fixedCost` for same-chain swaps. When both fields are present, `oracleCosts` takes precedence.

inputOracle.description: Oracle contract address on `fromChain`. Together with `outputOracle`, it identifies the pair priced by this entry. EVM (eip155): 0x-prefixed 40-char hex. Solana: 32–44 char base58. Tron: base58check, T-prefixed, 34 chars.

outputOracle.description: Oracle contract address on `toChain`. Together with `inputOracle`, it identifies the pair priced by this entry. EVM (eip155): 0x-prefixed 40-char hex. Solana: 32–44 char base58. Tron: base58check, T-prefixed, 34 chars.

fixedCost.description: Total fixed cost for this oracle pair in fromAsset raw base units

ranges.description: Array of quote ranges with different price tiers. At most 1000 ranges per quote. Ranges with the same route, `integratorKeyHash` and `exclusiveFor` must not overlap, including ranges in other quotes in the request. A range can start at the previous range's `maxAmount`. Ranges with identical bounds do not count as overlapping, and the last one is used. A request with overlapping ranges is rejected with 400.

expiry.description: Expiry timestamp in Unix seconds. Quotes that have already expired on receipt are skipped.

exclusiveFor.description: Exclusive solver address allowed to fill this quote. The address format follows fromChain. EVM (eip155): 0x-prefixed 40-char hex. Solana: 32–44 char base58. Tron: base58check, T-prefixed, 34 chars. Without it, any solver can fill orders opened from this quote, and they still count toward the quoting solver's reputation with the same fill window. An order another solver fills first within that window counts as neither a fill nor a miss.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier for this input (e.g., "eip155:1"). Applies to both user and asset.

user.description: Native address of the user providing the input assets. Solana users may be wallets or PDAs.

asset.description: Address of the token/asset being provided as input.

amount.description: For exact-input, the amount to provide in base units, written as 1 to 78 digits and no larger than 2^256 - 1. Ignored for exact-output.

lock.description: Optional lock reference for securing the input assets. Shape: { kind: "the-compact" | "rhinestone", params: object }. Currently ignored by the quote decoder.

inputs.description: Available inputs for the quote. Order is significant if preference is input-priority.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier for this output (e.g., "eip155:1"). Applies to both receiver and asset.

receiver.description: Native address that will receive the output assets

asset.description: Address of the token/asset to be received as output.

amount.description: For exact-output, the amount to receive in base units, written as 1 to 78 digits and no larger than 2^256 - 1. Ignored for exact-input.

calldata.description: Optional calldata describing how the receiver will consume the output. Enables composability with other protocols

swapType.description: Swap type for the quote. exact-input: quotes are based on inputs[].amount and outputs[].amount is ignored. exact-output: quotes are based on outputs[].amount and inputs[].amount is ignored. If none available, return []

minValidUntil.description: Minimum validity timestamp in unix timestamp (seconds). Only select solver quotes with longer TTL.

originSubmission.description: Explicit preference for submission responsibility and acceptable auth schemes. Shape: { mode: "user" | "protocol", auth?: string[] }. Unsupported, ignored for now - needs gasless feature.

failureHandling.description: Failure handling policy for execution that the integrator supports (unsupported, ignored)

partialFill.description: Whether the integrator supports partial fills. Partial fills are not supported - if true, return quotes: []

metadata.description: Metadata for the order, never required, potentially contains provider specific data

exclusiveFor.description: Restrict quote lookup to quotes belonging to the specified solver(s). Accepts a single solver address or an array of solver addresses. Each address must use the native address format of the corresponding input chain; for requests with multiple input chains, an address applies only to compatible input-chain candidates. If omitted, the best available quote across all whitelisted solvers is returned. If provided, only quotes whose exclusiveFor matches one of the given addresses are considered; if none exist or are acceptable, an empty quotes array is returned.

oracle.description: Accepted oracle deployment addresses, identified by chain and address. When provided, both addresses of the oracle pair selected for the quote must appear in this list under their respective source and destination chains. For cross-chain Polymer routes with EVM or Tron on both sides, the order encodes the source oracle in both inputOracle and outputs[].oracle. The destination entry still identifies the destination deployment, which can differ from the encoded output oracle and response metadata.oracle.output. Contracts marked as retired are excluded. Omit or pass an empty list to use the configured oracle pairs. Ignored for same-chain swaps.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier, e.g. "eip155:1"

address.description: Native contract address for the chain

inputSettler.description: Accepted input settler contracts, each a { chain, address } object. When provided, a quote is only returned if the order is built with one of these input settlers and the winning solver supports it. Omitted or empty means any input settler is acceptable.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier, e.g. "eip155:1"

address.description: Native contract address for the chain

sponsor.description: Optional fee/rent sponsor for the origin `open` transaction, as a { chain, address } object. Solana origin only. When set, the returned unsigned transaction uses this address as fee payer and rent payer, and both the sponsor and the user must sign it. Defaults to the input user.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier of the sponsor. Must match the input chain. Only Solana origins are supported.

address.description: Native address of the sponsor wallet. Must be an on-curve signing wallet (not a PDA).

outputSettler.description: Accepted output settler contracts, each a { chain, address } object. When provided, a quote is only returned if the order is built with one of these output settlers and the winning solver supports it. Omitted or empty means any output settler is acceptable.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier, e.g. "eip155:1"

address.description: Native contract address for the chain

intent.description: Intent details for the quote request

supportedTypes.description: Order types supported by the provider. If provided, only return quotes if "oif-user-open-v0" is contained, otherwise return []

rfqEnabled.description: When true, solvers are also asked to quote this request directly, which can make the response slower. Applies only to requests with one input and one output and without an integrator key. Defaults to false.

rfqMaxWaitMs.description: Longest time in milliseconds to wait for solvers to quote this request directly. Must be a whole number from 1 to 5000, also when rfqEnabled is false or missing. Used only when rfqEnabled applies. It never turns it on or changes which solvers are asked. Defaults to 200 for same-chain and 400 for cross-chain requests. A supplied value replaces the default, also when it is larger. The wait ends early once every asked solver has answered. It limits only this wait, not the total response time.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier for the destination contract

gasRequired.description: Gas required for execution as a decimal string

value.description: Native value in wei to attach to the transaction, as a decimal string. Present only when the intent input is the native token.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier (Solana namespace)

data.description: Base58-encoded serialized VersionedTransaction. The dummy all-zeros recentBlockhash must be replaced with a fresh blockhash before signing.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier (Tron namespace)

data.description: Full ABI calldata (selector + args) as a 0x-prefixed hex string. Pass it as `data` (without the 0x prefix) to the fullnode HTTP endpoint wallet/triggersmartcontract, or with tronweb 6.x as `triggerSmartContract(to, "", { feeLimit, input: data }, [], owner)`.

feeLimit.description: Suggested fee_limit in SUN as a decimal string. A cap on energy spend, not an estimate.

value.description: Native TRX value in SUN to attach as call_value in the TriggerSmartContract envelope, as a decimal string. Present only when the intent input is native TRX.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier (Stellar namespace)

data.description: Base64 XDR of the `Order` ScVal. Decode it into a ScVal and pass it as the only argument to `open` on `to`. Build the transaction with the user as its source, simulate it, assemble it from the simulation result, then sign and submit it. The escrow derives the order ID from these exact bytes, so keep them to track or refund the order.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier for this allowance check (e.g., "eip155:1")

token.description: Token contract address in the chain-native rendering

required.description: Required allowance amount as string-encoded integer

allowances.description: Required allowances and balances. Each item asserts that user has at least required balance and allowance for spender on token. No allowance is provided for native tokens, native tokens must be provided as transaction value.

type.description: Order type identifier for user open intent execution

openIntentTx.description: Open intent transaction. EVM produces hex calldata; Solana produces a base58 serialized VersionedTransaction whose recentBlockhash must be overwritten before signing. For a Solana PDA user, this transaction is an instruction template that must be converted to CPI by the controlling program, not submitted directly. Tron produces hex calldata the client wraps in a TriggerSmartContract envelope. Stellar produces the base64 XDR order the client passes to the escrow function `open` in a transaction it builds, simulates and signs.

checks.description: Allowance and balance checks that must hold prior to execution. `allowances` is empty for Solana and Stellar origins. Solana transfers SPL tokens inside the open instruction. On Stellar the user authorizes the token transfer as part of `open`.

types.description: EIP-712 types used to construct the digest

since.description: When the exemption from automatic pauses started

misses.description: Misses counted when the pause started. For a TrialMiss pause, the missed orders of the trial

orders.description: Orders counted when the pause started, or null when no order count was recorded. For a TrialMiss pause, the trial orders that have an outcome

chain.description: CAIP-2 ID of the destination chain the pause applies to, or null when it applies to every destination chain

cause.description: Why the pause started. RecentMisses: too many misses in the recent window. ConsecutiveMisses: too many misses in a row. TrialMiss: a miss during a trial. Manual: paused by the LI.FI team.

plannedEndAt.description: When the pause is planned to end, or null when it has no planned end. A pause stays in force past this time until it has ended.

endedAt.description: When the pause ended, or null while it is in force

trigger.description: Miss counts recorded when the pause started, or null when none were recorded

phase.description: CollectingFills while the trial still needs fills. AwaitingOutcomes once the fill target is reached and the trial waits for its remaining trial orders to resolve.

fills.description: Trial orders filled within their exclusive window

fillTarget.description: Fills needed to finish the trial. The trial ends once its remaining trial orders resolve.

outstanding.description: Trial orders that still hold a slot. An order holds a slot from when it opens on chain until it is filled or its exclusive window ends.

maxOutstanding.description: Most trial orders that can hold a slot at once. Orders from quotes returned earlier can still arrive and go above it.

windowHours.description: Length of the recent window in hours

since.description: Start of the counted period. This is the window start, or a later time when the scope recovered from a pause inside the window.

orders.description: Orders counted since the start of the counted period

pauseAt.description: Misses that start a pause at the current number of counted orders. It changes as orders are counted and as old orders leave the window.

misses.description: Misses in a row since the last filled order, counting only orders opened since the latest pause in this scope ended. Orders without an outcome yet are skipped.

pauseAt.description: Misses in a row that start a pause

windowDays.description: Length of the long-term window in days

orders.description: Orders counted in the long-term window

baselineMisses.description: Baseline misses added to the recorded misses for this daily calculation

baselineOrders.description: Baseline orders added to the counted orders for this daily calculation

adjustedRate.description: (misses + baselineMisses) / (orders + baselineOrders), using the baselines saved with this daily calculation. Multiply by 100 for a percentage.

updatedAt.description: When the long-term numbers were last calculated

status.description: What applies to orders in this scope. Paused if this scope or the whole solver has a pause in force. Otherwise Trial if either has an open trial, or Unrestricted if neither does. Unrestricted does not guarantee that a quote is selected.

pauses.description: Pauses in force that were started for this scope, oldest first

trial.description: The open trial for this scope, or null when none is open

recentMisses.description: Misses in the recent window, or null when no calculation is available

consecutiveMisses.description: Misses in a row, or null when no calculation is available

longTermMisses.description: Misses in the long-term window from the latest daily calculation, or null before the first calculation or when it found no orders with an outcome in this scope
